verification.note: migrated from data/antibiogram-raw.json: extracted from the source PDF, then re-verified cell by cell by a second reader (2026). Reading method: Text-extractable PDF (PyMuPDF), 6 pages. Method: The band table is Table 3 (page 4); isolate numbers are the Table 2 ICU totals per genus. The 'cephalosporins (1st to 3rd generation)' band is recorded under ceftazidime and ceftriaxone. Where Table 3 and the text disagree, Table 3 was followed (E. coli cefoperazone-sulbactam under 60% in the table, 60 to 80% in the text; Klebsiella nitrofurantoin effective in the table, low in the text). Nitrofurantoin and norfloxacin, listed as effective for Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter in Table 3 but inadequate in the page 3 text, were left out. Enterobacter (n=15) and single Stenotrophomonas and Burkholderia isolates had no per-drug results.

notes: Padmaja et al. (Bioinformation 2025) studied Gram-negative isolates from the ICUs (MICU, SICU and CCIU) of Konaseema Institute of Medical Sciences, Amalapuram, June 2023 to July 2024. The paper gives no exact percentages, only bands for urinary isolates: 80% or more, 60 to 80%, and under 60%. A figure of 70 marks the 60 to 80% band, not a measured value; under-60% results carry no number; P. aeruginosa meropenem 80 comes from the text. The only exact figure is Acinetobacter tobramycin, 96%. Isolate numbers (K. pneumoniae 277, E. coli 244, P. aeruginosa 148, A. baumannii 93, Proteus 13) count all ICU isolates, not urinary ones, and the paper names only genera, shown here as the main species. Carbapenem results are for meropenem, the only carbapenem tested. The paper contradicts itself on some urinary agents, for example nitrofurantoin for Klebsiella.
issues: This is a banded/qualitative antibiogram, not numeric. Table 3 gives ranges (>=80% highly, 60-80% moderately, <60% poorly). The extraction represents the 60-80% band as s=70 (midpoint) and flags approx=true; the 80% cell (Pseudomonas carbapenems) as s=80; and <60% cells as s=null. MINOR over-specification: the paper names organisms only at genus level for the ICU cohort (Klebsiella, Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, Proteus). The extraction assigns species (K. pneumoniae, P. aeruginosa, A. baumannii, P. mirabilis). These are reasonable inferences (species named elsewhere in discussion) but are not stated for the antibiogram itself. No susceptibility impact.

All n values, band assignments, and drug mappings verified correct against Table 2 and Table 3. Meropenem <60% for Acinetobacter (explicit in Table 3 poorly-sensitive column), Tobramycin 96% for Acinetobacter, and Pseudomonas carbapenems 80% are all accurately captured. No hallucinated cells and no %R<->%S direction errors.
